HOW TO SUBMIT A GRANT APPLICATION?

  1. Complete and submit your application using the online application form. Log in at https://www.palyazat.gov.hu via the "Single sign-on Interface Login" button to access the e-Government (EPTK) system.

A user manual illustrating the use of the Unified Institutional System Interface is available at https://help.fair.gov.hu/node/427.

HOW ARE SUBMITTED GRANT APPLICATIONS EVALUATED?

  1. continuously check the eligibility of applications received in each phase according to the eligibility criteria specified in the call.
  2. submit eligible applications for content evaluation on an ongoing basis.
  3. make grant decision in each phase in order of the scores achieved during the evaluation.

Applicants are advised to monitor announcements and system messages. Notifications about budget monitoring are sent only to businesses that have started completing their grant application.

Details are included in the call for proposals entitled Enhancing the Cybersecurity Capabilities of the Domestic SME Sector, code SSNS-NCC-HU-FSTP-2026. The call can be downloaded from the official website of NCC-HU and from the website https://www.palyazat.gov.hu.

If you have any questions or comments regarding the call for proposals, please contact the NCC-HU customer service at ncc-ih@nbsz.gov.hu.
description:
WHO CAN SUBMIT A GRANT APPLICATION?

Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises may submit grant applications for the call if they:

  1. have at least three closed financial years (each supported by financial statements and covering full 365-day period of operation as a pre-company is not included);
  2. operate in the sectors listed in Annexes 2 or 3 of the Cybersecurity Act

WHAT ACTIVITIES ARE ELIGIBLE FOR SUPPORT?

  1. Acquisition of new equipment and intangible assets resulting in the enhancement of cyber resilience
  2. Centralised endpoint protection solutions (traditional antivirus);
  3. Advanced endpoint protection and incident detection solutions (EDR/XDR);
  4. Perimeter protection solutions (firewall, Web Application Firewall, proxy, VPN gateway);
  5. Network traffic monitoring and intrusion detection solutions (WAF, IDS/IPS, NDR);
  6. Solutions against denial-of-service attacks (Anti-DDoS);
  7. Data backup and recovery solutions (backup/restore);
  8. Centralised log collection solutions (log management);
  9. Advanced log analysis solutions;
  10. Security information and event management solutions (SIEM);
  11. Mobile device management solutions (MDM);
  12. Multi-factor authentication solutions (MFA);
  13. Identity and access a management solutions (IAM);
  14. Data loss prevention solutions (DLP);
  15. Anti-spam and e-mail security solutions;
  16. Governance, risk and compliance management solutions (GRC);
  17. Encryption and key management solutions;
  18. Replacement of hardware or software components that are no longer supported by security update (obsolete hardware/software).
  19. Procurement of Services related to the enhancement of cyber resilience:
  20. Cybersecurity testing and assessment services (vulnerability testing);
  21. Cybersecurity Operations Centre (SOC) services;
  22. Cybersecurity-related training activities;
  23. Subscriptions to cybersecurity training platforms;
  24. Integration of hardware and software tools (system design, implementation, configuration, testing and documentation);
  25. Cybersecurity-related consulting and professional advisory services.

Details are included in the call for tenders!

callTitle: Enhancing the Cybersecurity Capabilities of the Domestic SME Sector (SSNS-NCC-HU-FSTP-2026)
furtherInformation:
The purpose of this call for proposals is to enhance the cybersecurity resilience and risk management capabilities of the domestic SME sector, thereby contributing to the objectives of the European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre (hereinafter: ECCC) as set out in the Digital Europe Cybersecurity 2025-2027 Work Programme.

Under this call for proposals:

  1. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) may submit grant applications without territorial restrictions;
  2. Applications must comply with the limitations specified in the call;
  3. Eligible applicants are those operating in the sectors listed in Annexes 2 or 3 of Act LXIX of 2024 on Cyber Security in Hungary.

Call for proposals

  1. Managing authority: NCC-HU;
  2. Funding source: Digital Europe Programme and the Hungarian State budget, through NCC-HU call for proposals DIGITAL-ECCC-2024-DEPLOY-NCC-06;
  3. Evaluation procedure: applications will be evaluated in stages with funding decisions taken in order of the scores achieved within each stage.

Rules and Regulations

The detailed rules on how the NCC-HU manages and uses the are set out in Government Decree No. 474/2025. (XII. 30.) on the detailed rules for the activities of the National Coordination Centre (hereinafter: Government Decree). Applicants are hereby informed that the following documents jointly contain all conditions necessary for preparing and submitting a grant application:

  1. the call for proposals,
  2. the Government Decree,
  3. the General Terms and Conditions (hereinafter: GTC),
  4. the NCC-HU Accounting Guide (hereinafter: Accounting Guide),
  5. the grant application form and its annexes.

The managing authority reserves the right to amend the documents. Any amendments will be published and applicants are requested to regularly monitor the official website of the NCC-HU and on the palyazat.gov.hu for updates.

The managing authority may set stricter requirements in the call for proposals than those laid down in the general rules of the Accounting Guide. In the event of any discrepancy between the provisions of the call for proposals and the general provisions of the Accounting Guide, the provisions of the call for proposals shall prevail.

The financing of activities eligible under this call for proposals shall be considered State aid within the meaning of Article 107(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU).

Such aid maybe implemented in compliance with EU competition law under the following categories of aid and applicable rules:

  1. General de minimis aid (EU) Commision Regulation 2023/2832

Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants

Under this call, Phortify internships refer to short-term, practice-oriented placements, as foreseen in the Phortify Grant Agreement. They are learning-based activities and do not constitute employment.

The Phortify Internship Grants support both students enrolled in Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes and students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s programme, provided that the internship is Phortify-labelled, aligned with the objectives of the Phortify project, and carried out in accordance with the Phortify Grant Agreement.

Participating partners:

Activer Fiber Systems (AFS):

- https://www.afs-jena.de/

ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences:

- https://www.icfo.eu/

Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e):

- Master of Science in Applied Physics

- Master of Science in Electrical Engineering: track (1) Semicon Devices and track (2) Connected World Technologies

Warsaw University of Technology (WUT):

- Master of Science in Mechatronics

- Master of Science In Photonics

Friedrich Schiller University (FSU):

- Master of Science in Photonics

- Master of Science in Quantum Science & Technology


How to apply for funding

Funding opportunities will be advertised through (1) the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, (2) the official Phortify website (https://phortify.eu/my-phortify/) and (3) the official Phortify partner websites.

Applications for Phortify funding must be submitted via the Phortify website. Applicants are required to consult the dedicated MyPhortify page, where all funding opportunities available under this pilot call are listed together with detailed application instructions and links to the relevant local application forms.

Nationality eligibility

  1. Applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, an associated country, or a country with which the European Union has an ongoing cooperation agreement under the Digital Europe Programme.
  2. Eligible countries include, inter alia, countries participating in Digital Partnerships, Trade and Technology Councils, digital dialogues, or other forms of ongoing international cooperation with the European Commission in the field of digital technologies.

The authoritative list of eligible countries will be published as part of this call and may be updated in accordance with European Commission guidance.

Eligibility

Under this call, Phortify Internship Grants may be awarded to students belonging to one of the following categories:

Category A – Phortify master degree-seeking students

Students who are enrolled in one of the Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes offered by the consortium universities and who undertake a Phortify-related internship during their period of study.

Category B – Phortify non-degree seeking students participating in Phortify student activities

Students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s Degree Programme but who participate in a Phortify-labelled internship, as foreseen under the Phortify Grant Agreement and implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

In all cases, eligible applicants must be students at the time of the internship, and the internship must:

  1. be directly related to the thematic areas and objectives of the Phortify project;
  2. contribute to the academic and professional development of the student;
  3. be carried out during the student’s period of study;
  4. be implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

Applicants must submit the following documentation:

  1. Latest official academic BSc and MSc (if applicable) transcripts
  2. A Phortify-specific motivation letter, describing the applicant’s motivation for applying for Phortify funding and their alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project
  3. A curriculum vitae (CV)

Applications that fail to meet the minimum eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation will be declared ineligible and will not be further evaluated.

Evaluation and selection

The predefined evaluation framework applicable to this call is published on the Phortify website as a dedicated evaluation framework document and applies to all partner institutions.

1. Purpose and Scope

This description defines the evaluation framework applied to applications submitted under the Phortify Internship Grants – Pilot Call.

The framework ensures transparency, equal treatment of applicants, consistency across partner institutions, and alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project, including its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) principles.

2. Evaluation Principles

The evaluation process is based on the following principles:

  1. Transparency and traceability of decisions
  2. Equal and fair treatment of all applicants
  3. Merit-based selection
  4. Consideration of DEI objectives in line with EU guidance

3. Evaluation Process Overview

The evaluation consists of two sequential stages:

  1. Eligibility verification (pass/fail)
  2. Comparative assessment and ranking

4.  Stage 1 – Eligibility Verification

Applications are checked for compliance with all eligibility requirements defined in the call text. Applicants must submit all required supporting documentation, including academic transcripts, a Phortify-specific motivation letter, and a curriculum vitae (CV).

Applications that fail to meet the eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation are declared ineligible and are not further evaluated.

5.   Stage 2 – Comparative Assessment

Eligible applications are assessed comparatively using the criteria below. Each criterion is scored independently on a scale from 0 to 5 points.

Evaluation Criteria

  1. Academic Excellence (0/5): Academic performance, relevance of previous studies, and preparedness for the proposed internship.
  2. Motivation and Alignment with Phortify Objectives (0/5): Quality, coherence, and relevance of the motivation letter, including alignment with Phortify’s educational and societal objectives.
  3. Overall Applicant Profile (0/5): Skills, experience, background, and potential contribution to the Phortify community, as reflected in the CV.

Maximum total score: 15 points.

Ranking and Allocation of Funding

Funding under this call is awarded following a rolling call procedure. Applications may be submitted at any time while the call is open. Applications are evaluated at regular intervals, typically every 2 to 3 months, or earlier if the number of submitted applications or budget availability so requires.

Following each evaluation round, eligible applications are ranked in order of merit, and funding is allocated until the available budget under this call is exhausted. In cases of oversubscription, priority is given to higher-ranked applications. Where applications receive identical or comparable evaluation results, tie-break rules promoting underrepresented groups, including women and students from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds, will be applied in line with Phortify DEI objectives.

Selection Committees

Applications are evaluated by local selection committees established by the Phortify partner institutions. Committees apply this evaluation framework consistently and impartially. Members must declare any conflicts of interest and ensure appropriate mitigation measures.

Documentation and transparency

Evaluation outcomes and funding decisions are documented by the partner institutions. Awarded grants are communicated to the Phortify Coordinator. Aggregate data will be reported in accordance with the project’s reporting obligations.

Available funding under this call

Type and duration of financial support

Financial support under this call is provided either as a monthly allowance or as a lump sum, depending on the Phortify partner institution.

Monthly allowances are paid for the actual duration of the internship, subject to partner-specific conditions. Lump-sum grants are not linked to a fixed duration and are intended to contribute to the overall costs associated with the internship, such as travel, accommodation, and subsistence.

AFS:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.200/month for master students

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 800/month for bachelor students

ICFO:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 600/month for a maximum duration of 6 months

TU/e:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

WUT:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

FSU:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.500 - lump sum not linked to duration


Financial support may only be used for the activities listed above; no other activities are eligible.
description:
About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

The objective of the Call for thematic grants is to support experience sharing between CSOs that work on behalf of groups at risk of discrimination, unequal treatment, hate speech or hate crime, or that carry out watchdog/monitoring/advocacy activities in support of respect for the rule of law, or that aim to gain experience in these areas within the project.

Experience sharing grants are meant to enable peer learning between two CSOs (Applicant and Partner) of different levels of experience regarding human rights and/or rule of law activities, organisational development, team building, etc. They are intended to encourage CSOs to share skills and solutions.

Total budget for the call: PLN 300 000 approx. EUR 69 460)

Minimum/maximum grant amount: PLN 10 000-20 000 (approx. EUR 2 315-4 600)

In order to be eligible, Applicants must:

- Be established in Poland.

- Be non-profit making and a civil society organisation.

- Respect EU values as laid down in Art.2 of the Treaty on European Union and the EU Charter of fundamental rights.

- Have eligible legal form: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, so called ordinary associations

- Have been registered at least 12 months before submitting the application.

I order to be eligible Partners must:

- Be established in Poland.

- Be non-profit making and a civil society organisation.

- Respect EU values as laid down in Art.2 of the Treaty on European Union and the EU Charter of fundamental rights.

- Have eligible legal form: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, so called ordinary associations.

Only activities taking place in an EU Member State are eligible.

Submitted proposals will be evaluated in an open-end (rolling) call. Grants will be awarded a maximum of four times (until the allocation is exhausted), according to the following schedule:

- until December 19, 2025,

- until April 30, 2026,

- until September 4, 2026,

- until December 18, 2026.

Eligible types of project activities:

• study visits;

• joint workshops;

• job shadowing;

• traineeships;

• exchange of experts between Applicant and Partner;

• joint initiatives testing new working methods. Organisations cannot conduct religious worship as part of the project, and funded activities must not directly or indirectly promote religious doctrine, mission or appeal to a particular faith.

Further information, including a detailed description of the call procedure, can be found on the Equal Rights Programme website: https://programrownychpraw.batory.org.pl/.
